name: Joe William Waters
summary: Physicist and engineer known for microwave remote sensing of Earth's atmosphere and development of the Microwave Limb Sounder.

name: Peter H. Siegel
summary: Author of the biographical article and colleague at Caltech/JPL.

name: Jamie Waters
summary: Father of Joe William Waters, a farmer.

name: Sarah Waters
summary: Mother of Joe William Waters, a local school teacher.

name: Dave Staelin
summary: MIT professor and Joe Waters' PhD supervisor and lifelong mentor.

name: Alan Barrett
summary: Founder of the MIT radio astronomy group and Waters' professor.

name: Frank Barath
summary: Microwave engineer at JPL who led instrument development for Nimbus-5.

name: Massachusetts Institute of Technology
summary: University where Waters earned his BS, MS, and PhD degrees.

name: Jet Propulsion Laboratory
summary: NASA research center where Waters worked from 1973 until retirement.

name: NASA
summary: US space agency that funded and launched Waters' satellite instruments.

name: Pasadena
summary: Location of JPL where Waters worked.

name: Nimbus-5
summary: NASA satellite launched in 1972 carrying a microwave spectrometer Waters worked on.

name: Microwave Limb Sounder
summary: Instrument series developed by Waters for measuring atmospheric composition.

name: Upper Atmosphere Research Satellite
summary: NASA satellite launched in 1991 carrying the first MLS instrument.

name: EOS Aura
summary: NASA satellite launched in 2004 carrying the EOS MLS instrument.
